history.heading: Dutch side of the island
paragraphs: Sint Maarten is the southern Dutch part of an island in the northeastern Caribbean, shared with the French Collectivity of Saint Martin. The Dutch were attracted by its salt ponds in the 17th century. After Spanish occupation, the Netherlands and France divided the island in 1648 in the Treaty of Concordia.

Plantations and salt production used enslaved Africans until slavery was abolished in 1863. Sint Maarten was part of the Netherlands Antilles until it became a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands on 10 October 2010. Hurricane Irma devastated the island in 2017.

culture.heading: Island culture
paragraphs: Dutch and English are official, and English is the main spoken language. The population is very diverse, with residents from across the Caribbean and the world. Carnival is a major event. Maho Beach is famous for planes landing just above sunbathers at Princess Juliana International Airport.

politics.heading: Constituent country
paragraphs: Sint Maarten is a self-governing country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands with its own parliament and prime minister. The Dutch monarch is represented by a governor, and the kingdom handles defence and foreign affairs.

economy.heading: Tourism
paragraphs: Tourism dominates the economy, including cruise ships, resorts, casinos and duty-free shopping. The currency is the Caribbean guilder, introduced in 2025, though US dollars are widely used.
